learning_outcomes.text: Know the techniques for surface analysis and characterization.
Acquire knowledge of the various surface modification and coating processes.
Learn to select the surface modification process based on the application.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Knowledge and abilities for the application of materials engineering.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Introduction. Surface preparation and surface characterization.
Topic 2. Study of surface degradation phenomena: Corrosion and wear.
Topic 3. Surface modification processes without changes in chemical composition: Thermal and mechanical processes.
Topic 4. Surface modification processes with changes in chemical composition: Thermochemical and physiochemical processes.
Topic 5. Surface modification processes through the application of coatings: Conventional techniques.
Topic 6. Surface modification processes through the application of coatings: Advanced techniques.
Topic 7. Surface modification processes through the application of organic coatings.
teaching_methods: Problem and case study solving sessions
Practical experiments: Surface preparation, coating generation, surface treatments with and without composition modification, degradation tests (wear, adhesion, corrosion)
assessment_rules: The final grade is a weighted average of all assessment activities, provided a minimum grade of 5.0 is achieved for re-evaluable components. If minimums are not met for some activities, the final grade will be the average of written tests, capped at 4.5. Laboratory practicals (25%) require a minimum grade of 5.0; failure or unjustified absence results in a "Fail" for the entire course. Students failing the ordinary call can retake only the re-evaluable components in the extraordinary call.
